dedupe_keys.name: dissecting the cost of peering global evidence from ixp port prices versus ip transit telecommunications policy 2026

description: This ISOC LIVE summary describes a paper by Anirudh Tagat and Amreesh Phokeer of the Internet Society, published in Telecommunications Policy (volume 50, 2026, article 103253, open access under CC BY-NC-ND and funded by the Internet Society), on the economics of peering at Internet exchange points. Using 2019 to 2024 data, it combines public IXP port prices from peering.exposed with proprietary TeleGeography IP transit prices, Packet Clearing House participant, traffic and bandwidth data, Internet Society Pulse indicators and ITU and Inclusive Internet Index variables, develops a simple model of an ISP choosing between peering and transit, and runs OLS and two-stage least squares models on broadband prices, mobile coverage, telecom revenues, ARPU and latency. It reports average peering cost of about USD 0.054 per Mbps a month against USD 18.2 for transit, and a survey of 20 IXPs found port fees were about 50 percent of peering-related costs; 'cost of peering' here means IXP port fees only. Producer: the Internet Society authors, with the summary posted on 9 June 2026; coverage is global, with about 1,051 IXPs as of March 2026. Access: the summary is free; the paper itself was not read. Licence and cost: CC BY-NC-ND per the summary, free. Caveats: the cost survey is a small non-representative sample, and figures come from a secondary summary. Simulation uses: the cost and savings figures give parameters for capacity-planning and investment models of interconnection. Related records: the PCH IXP directory (data-pch-ixp-directory), PeeringDB (data-peeringdb) and the ISOC assessment of IXP impact in Kenya and Nigeria (case_study-isoc-ixp-impact-kenya-nigeria-2012).
